page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the c4 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 62 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a single 402 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded performance in specific areas, such as text processing and gzip compression. Small-model LLM text generation also registers strong throughput. However, memory subsystem performance presents notable tradeoffs. While cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read bandwidth and the overall Passmark memory score fall into the bottom 25% tier. Other computational benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng, software compilation, and database operations, consistently perform in the average range.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, this server offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of a GPU. The inclusion of dedicated CPU cores and specialized cryptography and matrix multiplication hardware flags enhances its efficiency for secure, memory-intensive applications. It is well-suited for database operations, text processing pipelines, medium-scale web serving, and lightweight language model inference.
